### V · Carried from the v2 question list, 2026-09-11

- ▶ **Q-028** — CAN wake latency  
  *you*  
  waits also on install 5.4. record the wake-to-horn latency; nothing depends on it yet -- If the horn or the winks ever move to a CAN-node wake, what wake-to-horn latency is acceptable cold? Recorded so it is not rediscovered; on the current design nothing depends on it. Moved from the luxury package with its number (D-374).
- ▶ **V-002** — Alternator output rating  
  *you*  
  read the rating off the alternator tag -- The case reads only "B" / Mitsubishi. The 1980 and 1985 workshop manuals both give a 55 A Mitsubishi unit (`00-CAR/SPECS.md` SP-078, SP-079 — the 1985 part is A5T30574; the 1981–83 fiche lists N221-18-300R, SP-006); an enthusiast chart says 50 A for base cars (SP-080, unverified). Read the rating stamped on the case to settle which the 1982 GS automatic carries. Nothing in the harness depends on it — F18 is 100 A and the 6 AWG B+ cable carries 100 A — but the charging figures at install 2.14 cannot be called good or bad without it. It also feeds the D-179 no-charge diagnosis: D-198 rebuilt the excitation circuit, and this is the number that says whether a healthy unit is behaving.
- ▶ **W-330b** — Ask Ionic for the BLE protocol map for the IC-12V40-S9H, and for the S9H heater's own figures  
  *you*  
  Ask for the frame map on FFE0/FFE1: message types beyond 0x01, the command set for requesting current and state of charge, and the scale factors. Say the pack is an IC-12V40-S9H and that the type-01 cell frame already decodes at ~1.43 mV/count. This is what turns D-330 from voltage-only into the full picture without a shunt. **Second ask, added 2026-09-12 (V-052):** at what temperature the S9H's heater turns on and off, how much it draws, and whether it can draw from the pack itself or only from an active charging source. Self-heating packs of this class only heat while charging, which would take the heater off the sleeping budget entirely - but Ionic publishes nothing for the S9H, so it is unverified (00-CAR SP-233). One email, two answers.

- ⏳ **Q-110** — How long does the horn take from asleep?  
  *you* · waits on: C1 open  
  waits also on E25 (the PMU configured). a stopwatch measurement on a sleeping car -- Horn, hazard, wink — and now the brake (D-247 → D-278) — all work with the key out, and all of them work by *waking the module first*: the stage lifts pin 7, the PMU boots, decodes and drives the output. Nothing in the design says how long that takes, and the horn is the one control whose whole value is in its first 200 milliseconds. Measure it at §5.4 with a stopwatch and a helper: press the pad on a sleeping car, time until it sounds. Under ~200 ms, say nothing more about it. Over ~500 ms, decide whether the horn should hang off the always-hot busbar through its own relay instead — a change this build can still absorb and a finished car cannot. The brake is the same measurement and matters more.
- ⏳ **Q-115** — Road speed: the car may already have a signal, at the dash  
  *you* · waits on: C1 open  
  waits also on install M-6. a check at the speedometer head with the cluster out -- The speedometer is cable-driven and there is no electronic speed signal in the design - a digital cluster needs one. But the 1982 component list carries a **vehicle speed switch (B-29)**: a reed switch **inside the speedometer head** that pulses to ground on a single `BR` wire. It fed cruise control, which D-097 deleted, so it is sitting there unused and **terminating behind the dash**. **Check at M-6**, with the cluster out anyway: find the `BR` wire at the speedometer head, confirm it pulses to ground as the cable turns, and count pulses per wheel revolution. If it checks out, road speed costs **one conductor** into a free `L3-S2 12` or `L3-S3` cavity and the tunnel run is deleted from the plan. If it does not, the fallback is an inline pass-through sensor at the transmission (3-wire Hall, 12 V square wave, keeps the mechanical sp
- ⏳ **V-052** — The Ionic's heater trigger and winter draw  
  *agent* · waits on: W-330b open  
  Half answered 2026-09-12, and the half that matters is the good half. Self-heating LiFePO4 packs of this class draw the heater from an ACTIVE CHARGING SOURCE only - roughly -20 to +5 C on, off at +10 C - and take nothing from the pack when no charger is connected, so on this car the heater is NOT on the sleeping budget and V-052's premise dissolves. That is vendor-class behaviour, not Ionic's own sheet, which does not publish the S9H's figures: 00-CAR SP-233 carries it as unverified and the ask rides along with W-330b. Published and now recorded: 14.6 V ceiling (SP-231), 8.0 V cut-off (SP-232), -20 to 60 C operating.

### E · Then the install plan, in its own order

- ⏳ **E4** — Read the safety rules once, properly, before the first tool touches the car  
  *you* · waits on: D1 open; D4 open; C1 open; B1 open  
  The battery is lithium: boot or tape both terminals whenever you work, rings and watches off - a dropped tool welds. Open the master disconnect before touching the 2 AWG feed, the starter cable, the tank sender or the pop-up buckets. It is on the POSITIVE side (D-319), so opening it removes supply from everything, the starter cable included; before it is fitted, pull the negative lug. Jack stands always, wheels chocked (P is not a parking brake). No sparks near the tank; extinguisher within reach. Engine running: belt/fan clear, garage door open (CO). Pop-ups move fast and a stalled motor pulls 15-25 A. Label the factory end of every migrated circuit MIGRATED + date.
- ⏳ **E5** — Deutsch and heat-shrink practice on scrap  
  *you* · waits on: E4 open  
  Insert and remove a contact from a spare housing ten times with the removal tool (P031/P032); fit and pull the wedgelock - a contact must click and not back out under a firm tug. Adhesive heat-shrink until the glue weeps evenly at both ends; one lug with heavy-wall shrink and a boot.
- ⏳ **E2** — Read the factory odometer at the meters cutover (MG22) and record it  
  *you* · waits on: F3 open  
  Before the factory cluster goes dark at MG22 - the ICU's own odometer (D-269) starts from this figure. MG22 waits on the display proven on the bench, which is F3
- ⏳ **E6** — Set up the label printer and print the node labels  
  *you* · waits on: E5 open  
  Format: rules label-format. Print TEST / L0-X0, wrap it on a 16 AWG offcut, clear heat-shrink over it, tug it. Then print the node labels from the label columns: rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select id,label from relays" and "select id,label from fuses".
- ⏳ **E7** — Build the ladder resistor sub-assemblies  
  *you* · waits on: E6 open  
  Every resistor (and the one 1N5819) the ladders use, soldered to 4 in leads, each heat-shrunk and the lead labelled with switch and position; measure each and write the value on its bag. The list is the design, not this note: rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select * from ladders" plus the cavity rows naming a kΩ value. Includes the 47 kOhm baselines: L2-S 1 and 2 (A4/A5), and new with D-368 L2-S 3 (A3), the sill splice (A6) and the hazard switch (A8). Do not fit the D-368 baselines in the car until CK12 has passed on the bench (A10 sizes the wake stages first).
- ⏳ **E8** — Backbone weekend, 1 of 5: the battery in the cargo bin  
  *you* · waits on: E7 open  
  Disconnect the factory battery, negative first; boot the Ionic's terminals. Backing plate from the C1 (M-4) mock-up; hold-down through the floor with M8 grade-8, nyloc nuts, fender washers - never sheet metal alone. Fit battery and hold-down; push hard every way, it must not move (D2 fit-checked the parts).
- ⏳ **E9** — Backbone weekend, 2 of 5: disconnect, Class-T and the rear ground stud  
  *you* · waits on: E8 open  
  Master disconnect within reach from the hatch, on the POSITIVE side (D-319). Class-T block as close to the positive post as physically possible - inches. Rear ground stud: bare metal, 3/8 stainless stud, star washer, torque, cavity wax over the joint. Cut and hydraulically crimp the battery cables exactly as rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select * from backbone" and "select * from cables" route them (battery negative straight to the stud, B5); heavy-wall adhesive shrink and a boot on every lug.
- ⏳ **E10** — Backbone weekend, 3 of 5: starter run, PMU feed and grounds  
  *you* · waits on: E9 open  
  MRBF holder on the positive post with the 250 A fuse (D-321), NOT fitted yet; 1/0 starter run to the starter B+ stud (D-246), loomed, P-clipped every 12 in, grommeted at every pass-through. 2 AWG PMU feed from the Class-T through the tunnel to a temporary insulated distribution post where the dash node will go - pull string in beside it before the console goes back. Front star stud on the radiator support (bare metal, stud, star washer, torque, wax) + 10 AWG BLK to a second body bolt. Engine block to chassis strap, 2 AWG, 24 in or less (the bond). 1/0 BLK cranking return from the rear stud to the block with the starter feed (D-246). MIDI holders F17/F18 beside the starter stud; alternator B+ through F18; F17 unwired until E38.
- ⏳ **E11** — Backbone weekend, 4 of 5: the factory harness onto the new backbone, then power  
  *you* · waits on: E10 open  
  Move the factory harness's main feed (fusible-link side) onto the distribution post and its main ground onto the front star. Fit the Class-T fuse and the MRBF. Reconnect. Pair the Ionic app and record voltage ___ V, state of charge ___ %, temperature ___ C (into checks, CK02/CK03 as they apply).
- ⏳ **E12** — Backbone weekend, 5 of 5: start, charge, voltage drop, drive  
  *you* · waits on: E11 open  
  Start it. Charging voltage at the battery at 2,000 rpm: ___ V - expect 13.8-14.6; if it does not charge, stop - alternator or excitation (F15 fixes excitation at E39). Voltage drop while cranking (assistant on the key): battery + post to starter stud ___ V, battery - post to engine block ___ V, each under 0.5 V - near 0.5 means a bad crimp. Drive it: identical to before, on a new backbone.
- ⏳ **E13** — Dash node 1: lay it out with the parts in hand and cut the carrier panels  
  *you* · waits on: E12 open; C2 open  
  Inside a cardboard outline of C1's M-1 spaces place the PMU, the two busbars, blocks A and B, the inline holders, the relay sockets (rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select id from relays where location='Dash node'" - K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13), the wake strip, the perfboard (P134) and the wideband gauge. Rules: low and close to the floor; the PMU lever arc clear; 60 mm behind every receptacle; blocks reachable; the always-hot busbar covered; PMU stood off for airflow; no bare aluminium against a live stud. Mock the panels in cardboard IN THE CAR first; then cut, deburr, paint (panel stock P090 from C2).
- ⏳ **E14** — Dash node 2: mount everything and label every position  
  *you* · waits on: E13 open  
  PMU on three M6 stand-offs; covered always-hot busbar beside the stud; ground bus beside pin 25; blocks A and B; the sealed inline holders; the relay sockets; the 8-position barrier strip (P068 - full: seven wake inputs + the rail); the perfboard. Receptacle clips (P030) along the panel edge grouped by leg. Node labels from E6 beside every relay socket and fuse position, empty ones included.
- ⏳ **E15** — Dash node 3: the wake network and the two sense stages  
  *you* · waits on: E14 open  
  Seven 1N5819 on the strip, band (cathode) toward the common rail (N38); rail to pin 7; 10 kOhm rail to ground bus. The two NPN sense stages (door, A8) on the perfboard with the base-network values A10 writes into the record for D-368's baselines - not the v2 values. The two 100 kOhm bias resistors from pin 15 to pins 35 and 22. Then CK12 on the bench before the node goes in the car.
- ⏳ **E16** — Dash node 4: terminate the 39-way PMU connector  
  *you* · waits on: E15 open  
  Cavity order from rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select * from pins"; mark cavity 1 with the paint pen first. Strip, crimp the SICMA terminal (2.8 mm large for the heavy pins, 1.5 mm for the rest - per pins), tug, insert until it clicks, tug again; 18 in of wire on every pin; label each wire before cutting the next. Secondary lock on; pull every wire - none may move; latch the lever once fully to prove the arc is clear. It is terminated once and never reopened.
- ⏳ **E17** — Dash node 5: every node conductor, every receptacle  
  *you* · waits on: E16 open  
  Run every row of rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select * from node_conductors" - including the ones since v2: N73 road-speed supply, N74 the CAN2 120 Ohm terminator AT THE NODE (D-346), N75 F22 to DP-DCU 1 (D-355), N76-N78, N79 F13, N80-N83 the post links, N84 mirror heat from DP-DCU-B 9 to L4-P 4 (D-369), N85/N86 the release branch and select lines (D-370). O15 now feeds L3-P 2 only (D-369). Every splice a sealed crimp butt splice. Land every leg wire on its receptacle pin per cavities; sealing plug in every PLUG cavity; wedgelocks. Dust caps: the branch-end receptacles get theirs at E20-E23. DP-ICU-A/B are 150 mm tails into the ICU's DT13s (D-270); DP-DCU and DP-DCU-B are tails to the centre stack ending in DT06 plugs, dust-capped (P140, D-362) until the DCU plugs in at E26 (D-374).
- ⏳ **E18** — Dash node 6: continuity, isolation, relays, fuses, photos  
  *you* · waits on: E17 open  
  Continuity: each of the 39 cavities reaches every receptacle cavity, relay terminal or strip position the tables say, and nothing else (meter on beeper; touch three places it must NOT reach). Isolation: nothing plugged in, every adjacent pair of power cavities and each power cavity to the ground bus reads open (> 1 MOhm) - any reading is a stray strand. Fit relays K1 K2 K11 K12 K13 (P003) and the fuses per rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select id,rating,block,state from fuses"; empty positions stay empty and labelled (K3/K4 are the luxury package's, LP51). Every node wire labelled at both ends; photograph the finished panels from every angle.
- ⏳ **E19** — Dash node 7: the sleeping-current acceptance test (D-280)  
  *you* · waits on: E18 open  
  Node built, PMU asleep, meter in series in the main feed: ___ mA. Target 30 mA or less, accept 50 mA or less. Above that, pull wake-strip branches one at a time to find it. Do not close the dash on a failing number - it cannot be re-taken without undoing the install.
- ⏳ **E20** — Leg L3 dash: cut, pin, terminate, test  
  *you* · waits on: E19 open; G13 open  
  For every leg the same loop: lay the route full-scale from the routes table (G13 derives the lengths from C1's M-2); cut every wire in the leg's cavity rows to length + a 150 mm service loop, both ends labelled at once, CAPPED wires exactly like LIVE; crimp the socket contact (leg side = 06-...S housing), cavity order, click, tug; wedgelock; sealing plugs in PLUG cavities; device ends per the device-end rule (rules) using devices; grounds to their star; continuity end to end and the ladder check (switch through every position, ohms at the leg-side cavity vs ladders, within 2 %); tug every crimp; bundle every 150 mm, do NOT final-wrap. L3 specifics: the wiper stalk WASH contact carries both the 1.8 kOhm + diode leg and the plain wire to L3-S2 9; horn 8.2k and both wink NO resistors join onto L3-S1 11; each wink common to dash ground, its NC pole to its own L3-S1 wire; the hazard switch gets its 47k baseline (D-368). Branch ends: L3-CMF, L3-MOD, L3-RDR, dust-capped. L3-S2 3-6 and L3-S3 5-8 run on to DP-DCU-B at the centre stack (D-362).
- ⏳ **E21** — Leg L2 front: cut, pin, terminate, test  
  *you* · waits on: E20 open  
  Same loop as E20. Pop-up run feeds land per C1's M-3 ohm check (V-081) - DO NOT pin L2-P before that reading. The 47 kOhm baselines in the back of the L2-S plug to a ground ring on the front star: cavities 1 and 2 (A4/A5) and 3 (A3, D-368). Wiper park terminal L gets the 12k; LB capped. Horns get a ground ring under a mounting bolt. Branch end L2-OAT at the nose, dust-capped. (There is no L2-NZL - D-329.)
- ⏳ **E22** — Leg L4 rear + the sill node: cut, pin, terminate, test  
  *you* · waits on: E21 open  
  Same loop as E20. The fuel pump's return is its own 12 AWG to the rear stud, never shared. Sill node: D1/D2 receptacles pinned on the node side, door plugs filled with sealing plugs (RESERVED); ground stud; K5-K8 sockets empty (wired per D-363 - 85 and 87a to ground, 30 to the motor legs, 87 from F8/F9); F8/F9/F14 holders fitted empty (D-283). Door jamb switches: 33k (driver) and 8.2k (passenger) join L4-S 2 at the sill, and the 47k baseline to sill ground there (D-368). L4-M 3/4 run to the hatch and fuel-door solenoids (ring or spade to +; prove each solenoid's ground to the body with the meter) - switched later through K3/K4 (D-370). Branch end L4-RDR, dust-capped. Nothing runs through the door boots.
- ⏳ **E23** — Leg L1 engine: cut, pin, terminate, test  
  *you* · waits on: E22 open  
  Same loop as E20. Tach: the shielded cable (P074), drain to the dash node's ground bus at that end only, cut and insulated at the coil end. K9 on the inner fender in its weatherproof socket; its 10 AWG contact wires from F17 to the starter S terminal. Alternator plug: BW to L1-S1 2, WB to L1-S2 8. The ignition suppression condenser P135 on the coil branch at the coil bracket (D-281). L1-S1 9/10 are sealing plugs - the CAN2 terminator is at the dash node now (D-318, D-346). The LS reserves are pinned at the post, not run (D-271).
- ⏳ **E24** — Install 1: mount the node, first power-up through 5 A, laptop connected  
  *you* · waits on: E23 open  
  Mount the dash node; prove the lever and every receptacle can be reached. 2 AWG feed to the busbar lug, ground bus to the dash star, NO leg plugged in. First power-up through a 5 A inline bridged across the Class-T block's terminals, so a short melts a 5 A fuse, not 2 AWG. Fit DP-DIAG, laptop over CAN1. Power up with EVERY output disabled: no smoke, module visible. Then swap the 5 A for the Class-T fuse. The laptop is Camden's Windows laptop, kept only to run ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376).
- ⏳ **E25** — Install 2: enter the PMU configuration, outputs still disabled  
  *you* · waits on: E24 open  
  The configuration IS the record now (the v2 PMU-CONFIG-SHEET is archived): names and channels from pins, decode tables from inputs + ladders, expressions from logic, the retry classes from rules retry-class (MOTOR_BUS conditional, D-357), wake from rules, CAN from the CAN rows. Save as RevA-01. No limits yet.
- ⏳ **E26** — Install 3: plug in L3, the ICU and the DCU; read every input into its window  
  *you* · waits on: E25 open; F6 open  
  L3 plugged in; the ICU on its two DT13 tails, display on its ribbon; the DCU in its enclosure behind the centre stack on DP-DCU and DP-DCU-B with the panel on its ribbon (D-374) - its luxury loads are not there yet, so its outputs drive capped lines. Every output still disabled: key OFF/ACC/RUN/START, light switch, dimmer, pass, turn, hazard, wiper positions, wash, brake, horn, both winks, doors - write the reading into each decode window, then enter the tables. Every state must land in its window; anything between windows is a wiring fault to fix now. Then enter the enable-at limits from pins (enable_a). Still nothing enabled.
- ⏳ **E27** — Install 4: L2, L4 + sill and L1 into the car, loads still on the factory harness  
  *you* · waits on: E26 open  
  Route, P-clip, grommet and connect L2, L4 + sill and L1 at both ends with their loads still on the factory harness. Fit F17 and wire K9. The car must start and drive on the factory harness with everything in place.
- ⏳ **E28** — Install 5: migrate, one circuit per sitting, in the migration table's order  
  *you* · waits on: E27 open  
  Order: rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/00-electrical "select seq,id,circuit,ch from migration order by seq" (MG01 interior lamp first ... MG23 start last). The loop for every row: (1) unplug the load at its factory connector, label the factory end MIGRATED + date, tape it back; (2) connect it to the new harness; (3) enable that one output at its enable-at value; (4) operate it and read the live current in the client - that is the real measurement; (5) voltage at the device under load within 0.5 V of the busbar (return side within 0.3 V); (6) record it. On the first one (interior lamp) also set the limit to 2 A and short the output on purpose to watch the soft fuse trip and retry. Set every lamp channel's inrush window before enabling it. MG22 (the meters cutover) waits for F3 (display proven on the bench) and E2 (read the odometer first). Before stopping, EVERY day: the car starts and drives.
- ⏳ **E29** — Install 6: full function check and save the revision  
  *you* · waits on: E28 open  
  Every migration row done: every circuit in one pass - key out, ACC, RUN, engine running. Wipers LOW/HIGH/INT, park from both speeds, wash only while held; PARK/HEAD/dimmer/pass, pop-ups on HEAD, each wink alone with the key out; crank in P and N only; flasher rate, hazard override, the interior fade. Prove the limp-home procedure once (CK11, recovery RC01-RC08 as corrected by D-367). Save the configuration as a new revision.
- ⏳ **E30** — Factory harness out  
  *you* · waits on: E29 open  
  Every migration row done and every factory end labelled MIGRATED. Drive a week with the factory harness disconnected at both ends but still in the car. Then pull it out INTACT - do not cut it - with the factory fuse box, relays and control unit (the factory cluster leaves with it, D-268). Box it and keep it until after shakedown.
- ⏳ **E31** — Shakedown 1: cold, night, wet, long - with logging  
  *you* · waits on: E30 open  
  Cold start on a cold morning with logging on; watch the battery heater in the app and the voltage through crank. Night drive: park, head, high, pass, pop-ups, winks, every lamp, the display's dimming and tell-tales. Wet drive: wipers in every mode, park, wash. A long drive with logging; review every channel's peak current against its limit.
- ⏳ **E32** — Shakedown 2: tighten the limits to measured class values  
  *you* · waits on: E31 open  
  Every limit still at its channel cap goes to its measured class value (motors stall x 1.1, lamps x 1.35, resistive cold x 1.2, electronics x 1.5). Record the measured currents in loads.measured_a. Save as a new revision.
- ⏳ **E33** — Shakedown 3: re-torque, re-check, final-wrap, seal  
  *you* · waits on: E32 open  
  After the first heat cycles re-torque every lug and stud; re-check the voltage drop on the main feed and ground (E12's numbers). Now final-wrap the looms, tie down, seal every grommet.

  *you* · waits on: E33 open  
  Back up the final configuration. In the car: the limp-home kit (recovery RC rows, D-344), a printout of the pins and cavities tables, spare Deutsch contacts, the removal tools and five blade fuses of each value. The electrical project is then ready for CLAUDE.md §6.6 (as-built into 00-CAR, process to the archive).
